sources.title: About local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot
sources.locator: Local sandboxing; How it works; Configuring; Cross-platform support; Enterprise policy enforcement
sources.finding: Local sandboxing (CLI and app) is off by default and is lightweight OS process/filesystem containment via MXC, not a VM or container. It restricts filesystem paths, outbound and local network or per-host rules, and credentials: sandboxed tools get placeholders and a local proxy supplies real credentials only to approved HTTPS hosts. Built-in CLI file tools run in-process outside the OS sandbox and honour policy best-effort. The app can change sandboxing for an active local session. Managed settings can require sandboxing and fail closed when unavailable; /sandbox disable turns it off where policy permits bypass.

sources.title: About GitHub Copilot Memory
sources.locator: Types of memories; Where available; Storage and ownership; How memories are created; Reinforced and retired; Retention and expiry
sources.finding: Copilot Memory stores repository facts (shared with read-access collaborators, per repository, not pooled, not copied to forks) and user preferences, used across the app, CLI, code review, cloud agent, Mobile, Slack and Teams. Facts cite code and preferences cite the user's words; Copilot checks citations against the current branch and upvotes or downvotes memories. Memories cannot be created or edited directly on GitHub.com; CLI imports memories in bulk. Write-access users delete facts, users delete preferences, and Business/Enterprise admins can export or delete preferences. Default expiry is 90 days; owners can set 7-180 days for repository facts.

sources.finding: Prerequisites are a GitHub account, a Copilot plan or own model provider credentials, and Git. Onboarding signs in to GitHub (GHE.com hostnames supported; GHES accounts added later), offers a plan or a model provider, then connects repositories or local folders, including clones from other Git hosts. A session is started with a mode and prompt; Changes shows the diff and Create PR opens a pull request. Customize discovers and manages plugins, skills, MCP servers and canvases.

sources.title: Using Copilot cloud agent on GitHub Mobile
sources.locator: Starting a session; Assigning an issue to Copilot; Tracking sessions
sources.finding: On Mobile an issue is assigned to Copilot through its Assignees; sessions can be started from issues, PRs or repositories, and the session list can be searched and filtered, for example Open or Merged.

sources.title: Third-party coding agents
sources.locator: Introduction; Where you can use coding agents; Making coding agents available; Partner agents
sources.finding: Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex coding agents are public preview, run alongside Copilot, are started from the Agents tab, issues, PR mentions, Mobile or VS Code, and must be enabled by user, organization or enterprise policy. Enabling them installs a GitHub App for each agent and they can be powered by the existing Copilot subscription. They open PRs, request review and iterate on PR comments; they are separate agent sessions.

sources.title: Using Copilot cloud agent via the API
sources.locator: Agent tasks API; Authentication; Starting, listing, status; Issues API
sources.finding: Agent tasks API (public preview) creates, lists and gets tasks by ID; states are queued, in_progress, completed, failed, idle, waiting_for_user, timed_out and cancelled. It accepts only user-to-server tokens (PAT, OAuth app, GitHub App user token); installation tokens are unsupported. REST and GraphQL issue APIs (public preview) assign GitHub issues to Copilot with target repo, base branch, instructions, custom agent and model.

sources.title: Supported AI models in GitHub Copilot
sources.locator: Supported AI models; Model retirement history
sources.finding: Generally available models come from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, Moonshot AI and xAI. The retirement table lists models retired on 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-16 with suggested alternatives.

sources.title: Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot
sources.locator: Pricing tables; Copilot code review cost considerations
sources.finding: Model prices are per 1M tokens, for example Claude Sonnet 5.5 $2.00 input and $10.00 output. Copilot code review uses an undisclosed model and publishes only estimated typical credit ranges per review effort level.

sources.title: Accessing compliance reports for your enterprise
sources.finding: Enterprise settings provide downloadable SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, CSA CAIQ, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, CSA STAR and other reports from the Compliance page. The page does not state report periods or name Copilot scope.

sources.title: Adding sub-issues
sources.locator: Overview; Creating; Adding existing issues; GitHub CLI
sources.finding: Issues take up to 100 sub-issues per parent and eight nesting levels; existing issues, including from other repositories, can be added; projects can group and filter by parent. gh issue create --parent and gh issue edit --add-sub-issue manage them.

sources.title: Creating issue dependencies
sources.locator: Marking blocked by or blocking; GitHub CLI
sources.finding: Issues can be marked blocked by or blocking others; blocked issues show a Blocked icon on project boards and Issues pages; gh issue create/edit/view manage and read dependencies by issue number or URL.

sources.title: About GitHub Support
sources.finding: Paid plans, Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise contact GitHub Support directly; GitHub Free users use Community discussions except for account, security and abuse. Preview features and Copilot output correctness are out of support scope.

sources.title: The latest GitHub and GitHub Copilot SOC reports are now available
sources.finding: SOC 1, 2 and 3 reports covering Copilot Business and Enterprise apply to 2024-04-01 to 2024-09-30 and are available on the GitHub Enterprise Trust Center; Copilot gained Type II coverage after earlier Type I reports.

sources.title: Remote control for Copilot CLI sessions now generally available
sources.finding: Remote control streams a CLI session in real time to Mobile and github.com, supports non-GitHub repositories and directories without a repository, and lets users steer, review plans, stop the session, approve or deny permission requests and answer questions. Business and Enterprise need remote control and CLI policies enabled.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot app generally available
sources.finding: The app is GA on macOS, Windows and Linux; canvases are bidirectional surfaces where the user and agent operate on the same plan, pull request, terminal or browser session.

sources.title: Copilot automations
sources.locator: Overview; Availability and permissions; Personal and shared automations; Triggers; Billing; Proposed improvements; Security and safety
sources.finding: Automations run cloud agent on schedules, repository events or the API; they are managed from the Agents tab, the app, VS Code and the REST API. Write access is needed to create them. Shared automations act as Copilot, belong to the repository and keep working if the creator leaves; personal ones act as the creator, who cannot approve their PRs. Runs are visible to everyone with read access, including prompt, logs and changes. AI-credit limits: per run (minimum 30) stops a run; daily, weekly and monthly limits stop new runs but not running ones. Automations can propose changes to their own tools, triggers and prompts.

sources.title: Set AI credit session limits in Copilot CLI and SDK
sources.finding: CLI and SDK session limits (public preview) track AI credits across a session; /limits views or sets them and --max-ai-credits bounds a run. They are a soft cap that may be slightly exceeded and complement budgets.

sources.title: GitHub Mobile: Live notifications for Copilot CLI sessions
sources.finding: GitHub Mobile live notifications cover cloud coding agent sessions and remote CLI sessions, with states In progress, Waiting for user input, Idle and Finished.

sources.title: Upcoming changes to GitHub Copilot policies and billing
sources.finding: For card or PayPal customers, new Business and Enterprise seat assignments are paid upfront; revoking a seat gives no prorated refund. Unified Copilot on github.com retains chat data for the life of the account instead of 28 days.

sources.title: Client telemetry user attribution and configurable capture
sources.finding: In CLI, the app and VS Code Agent Host, OpenTelemetry identity capture (user.name, process.user.name, host.name) is off by default and separate from an existing pseudonymous identifier; prompt, response, tool argument, tool output and policy detail capture classes are each off by default and managed values take precedence.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot supports server-to-server authentication
sources.finding: In public preview, SDK services can use GitHub App installation tokens with the Copilot Requests organization permission; usage is billed to the organization, appears in AI usage CSV reports with app_client_id, and owners stop access by suspending or uninstalling the app.

sources.title: Agent Merge watches and fixes pull requests in the cloud
sources.finding: Agent Merge watches a PR and fixes failing Actions workflows, merge conflicts or both in a cloud environment, and can be combined with auto-merge; paid plans.

sources.title: Copilot code review: Merge with confidence with Max and approvals
sources.finding: Max effort (public preview) runs several independent review agents across providers plus an aggregation agent. Reviews include an approval assessment in the overview comment; approvals (GA, off by default) count toward required approvals and are dismissed when new commits are pushed. Admins set default and maximum effort and which paths Copilot may approve.

sources.title: github/gh-aw repository
sources.finding: GitHub Agentic Workflows repository is MIT licensed per repository metadata; latest prerelease v1.3.1 published 2026-11-18.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot app, Universe releases
sources.finding: App projects (public preview) hold repositories, design mocks, Slack threads and notes; Copilot coordinates agents in the background and checks in when it needs the user; focused single-repository sessions remain. Slack and Figma context and image generation are available.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot SDK is becoming Microsoft Copilot SDK
sources.finding: GitHub Copilot SDK is moving in phases to the Microsoft organization as Microsoft Copilot SDK; support stays the same.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile
sources.locator: Comparison of Actions-based sessions and cloud sandboxes; Access and availability; Ways to work; Session history; Customize; Limitations
sources.finding: Chat data is retained 28 days for Actions-based sessions and for the life of the account for cloud sandbox sessions. Without write access a session is read-only. Agentic work runs tests and linters; code review comments and suggests fixes. Hooks run commands during agent work; custom instructions (personal, repository, organization), custom agents and agent skills apply. Session logs show work and tools. Remote control keeps a CLI session on the local machine, which must stay online. Actions sessions support self-hosted runners and have a 59-minute limit. Copilot only works with GitHub-hosted repositories; new cloud experience requires a paid plan.

sources.title: Issue artifacts are now in public preview
sources.finding: Issue artifacts (public preview) attach Markdown, HTML and link artifacts to issues; app sessions attach artifacts automatically; gh issue artifact creates, edits, lists, views, downloads and deletes them, with image and video attachments; artifacts are edited on github.com with version history.

sources.title: New tools, triggers, and cost controls for Copilot Automations
sources.finding: Automations gain API triggers, issue triggers including closed, reopened and status changed, PR triggers, chaining, and tools to upload image or video attachments, merge PRs, mark PRs ready or draft and update comments; per-run, daily, weekly and monthly credit limits.

sources.title: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion
sources.finding: Copilot Fusion routes and orchestrates models per prompt (single, cascade, critique). GitHub reports a Fusion Max score of 60 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index without fixture or attempt detail.

sources.title: Work from anywhere with a new, connected Copilot cloud experience
sources.finding: One session continues across web, Mobile, app, VS Code and CLI with the same session list; sandboxes snapshot and resume. Mobile accepts voice and image input; Slack and Teams @GitHub create issues and sessions. Built-in connectors (Sentry, Linear, Cloudflare), key-auth MCP and skills apply. Chat sessions are scoped to one organization or personal repositories by default; enterprise agent permission and MCP allowlist settings apply. Paid plans only; Free keeps Copilot Chat.

sources.title: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available and more
sources.finding: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is GA; it creates issues, implements changes and opens PRs. Canvas in Teams shows plans, code changes and previews beside the discussion. Created issues and PRs say "Created from a Slack/Teams conversation with @username".

sources.title: Agent management
sources.finding: The Agents tab and Copilot home start sessions with Copilot, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI Codex or custom agents, show live session logs in real time, list active sessions, accept steering input mid-session, open a session in VS Code or Copilot CLI, and link to the resulting pull request for review and merge.

sources.title: GitHub Status incidents API
sources.finding: Status has Copilot and Copilot AI Model Providers components; recent incidents include critical 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-11 and major 2026-11-09 Copilot incidents.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
sources.locator: Where you can use MCP; Default MCP servers; Personal MCP servers; Repository-level configuration; Best practices
sources.finding: Cloud agent starts with the GitHub MCP server (read-only token scoped to the current repository by default) and Playwright (reads pages and takes screenshots on localhost). Connectors are GitHub-verified servers whose authentication GitHub handles. Personal MCP servers support key-based auth via COPILOT_MCP_ secrets and are only for the user. Repository administrators configure repository servers for everyone with write access; remote OAuth servers are unsupported there. The tools field allowlists tools; delegated work calls configured MCP tools without approval. The app discovers and installs MCP servers from Customize.

sources.title: Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent
sources.locator: Unvalidated code; Push changes; Sensitive information; Prompt injection; Auditability; Automations
sources.finding: Only write-access users trigger the agent and only their comments reach it. It pushes to one copilot/ branch or the PR branch it was asked on, subject to branch protection and required checks; it cannot mark PRs ready, approve or merge. Workflows wait for a write-access user to Approve and run. The requester cannot approve the PR; unattributed PRs need an extra approval. Internet access is firewalled. CodeQL, advisory and secret-scanning validation results and actions appear in the session log, and Copilot code review gives a second opinion. Commits are authored by Copilot with the requester as co-author, signed and Verified, and link to session logs; session logs and audit log events are available to administrators. Shared automations act as Copilot.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot CLI
sources.locator: Modes of use; Steering; Automatic context management; Customizing; Trusted directories; Allowed tools; Model usage; Using your own model provider
sources.finding: Interactive mode with plan mode; manual approval offers allow once, allow for the session (restored on resume) or reject with feedback. --allow-tool, --allow-all-tools and --deny-tool take shell(COMMAND), write and MCP tool specifications; deny takes precedence. /permissions assisted lets a model approve requests it judges safe. Trusted-directory scoping is heuristic. Auto-compaction runs at about 95% of the token limit; /context shows token usage. Custom instructions, custom agents, hooks, skills and Copilot Memory are supported; reasoning levels are configurable. BYOK connects OpenAI-compatible, Azure OpenAI or Anthropic endpoints, including local Ollama and vLLM.

sources.title: Custom agents
sources.locator: About agent profiles; Where you can use custom agents
sources.finding: Agent profiles are Markdown files with instructions that can restrict available tools and configure MCP servers; they are shared at repository, organization and enterprise level and used in the app, CLI, cloud agent and supported IDEs.
